name: Card-Not-Present & Online Card Fraud
summary: Card details harvested from phishing, skimming or breaches are used for online purchases where the physical card is never needed.

typicalLoss.note: Card fraud is often refundable if disputed promptly, which makes speed of detection the deciding factor.

targets: Anyone with a debit or credit card

howItWorks.detail: From a phishing page, a compromised online store, a skimmer, or a breached merchant database. You may never have done anything wrong.
A tiny transaction, often under R50 to a foreign merchant, confirms the card is live. This is the moment to catch it.
Once validated, purchases run quickly across digital goods, gift cards and gaming credit, which are easy to resell and hard to trace.
Either the merchant does not enforce it, or you were tricked into approving an OTP that you believed related to something else.

redFlags: Small unexplained transactions, especially to foreign or unfamiliar merchants.
OTPs arriving for purchases you did not initiate. Always read the merchant and amount.
Declined transactions on a card that should have funds.
Notifications of a changed delivery address or a new device on a shopping account.
illustrativeCase: A R14.90 charge to an overseas digital merchant appears on a statement and is dismissed as a subscription. Nine days later, R31 000 in gaming credit and gift cards is charged across six transactions in ninety minutes. The R14.90 was the live-card test.
howToProtect: Enable transaction notifications for every amount, including small ones, and actually read them.
Use a separate low-limit or virtual card for online shopping.
Read the merchant name and amount in every OTP message before approving.
Set an online purchase limit in your banking app.
Never save card details on sites you use rarely.
ifYouveBeenHit: Freeze the card in your app immediately, then call the bank.
Dispute the transactions in writing and ask for a chargeback. There are time limits, usually within 30 to 120 days.
Get a new card number rather than just a new PIN.
Open a SAPS case if the bank requires one for the dispute.

faqs.q: Will the bank refund unauthorised card transactions?
faqs.a: Often yes, where you did not authorise them and reported promptly. It is much harder if you approved an OTP, which is why reading OTP messages matters so much.

faqs.q: How did they get my card details if I never lost the card?
faqs.a: Most commonly from a breached merchant or a phishing page. The physical card is irrelevant to this type of fraud.
